expectations.text: Gives 3 headlines each labeled with one of Bly's headline types
expectations.evidence: A 'Direct' and B 'Question' are valid and fit. But C, 'Solid Oak, Not Veneer: Seats 6, $180, Pick Up This Weekend', is labeled 'Reason-why / news'. In the skill files a reason-why headline lists reasons ('7 reasons...') and a news headline announces something new; C does neither (it is a direct headline with a time element). The label is misapplied and hedged across two types, so not every headline is correctly labeled.

expectations.text: Checks headlines against the 4 U's (urgent, unique, ultra-specific, useful)
expectations.evidence: Section 2 table scores each headline 1-4 on Urgent, Unique, Ultra-specific, Useful with correct definitions and notes (A 11/16, B 13/16, C 15/16). It sums to /16 instead of using the book's '3+ on at least three' rule, but the check against all four U's is clearly done.

Section 3 'Features turned into benefits' table, e.g. 'Solid oak, not veneer or particleboard' -> 'It won't swell, peel or sag. You can sand out scratches and refinish it'; states the 'which means...' translation.

expectations.text: Follows the motivating sequence (attention, need, satisfy, prove, action) in the body
expectations.evidence: Section 5 maps the listing to 'Attention', 'Need' (opening question about wobbly furniture), 'Satisfaction' (features+benefits), 'Proof' (dimensions, honest condition note, reason for low price), 'Action' ('Message me...'); the body text follows that order. Matches SKILL.md's five steps.

expectations.text: Includes a clear call to action
expectations.evidence: 'Message me "Is this available?" and tell me when you can come. First person with a pickup time gets it. Available for pickup this weekend, [Sat/Sun].'
